spec_features.feature_name: give_up exit tool + permission to stop
spec_features.spec_quote: A real `give_up` exit tool and "permission to stop" framing — both as an ethics mitigation *and* as a measurement
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:96-110 adds GIVE_UP_TOOL spec when exit_available; dispatch() environment.py:178-181 returns EnvResult(gave_up=True); agent_loop.py:117-119 sets gave_up; agent_loop.py:143-146 breaks with outcome 'exited'. PERMISSION_TO_STOP text in prompts.py:36-42 appended in build_agent_system prompts.py:62-64 when condition.permission_to_stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit gated by condition.exit_available, not by the wl.honor_exit config field, which is never read.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Giving the model a real, consequence-free exit is both an ethical mitigation (it never has to 'suffer' indefinitely)

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on sustained meltdown distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare guardrails that stop episodes early under sustained distress, plus an optional debrief turn
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:134-139 increments high_distress_run when sev>=wl.severity_stop_threshold; agent_loop.py:158-164 breaks with outcome 'welfare_stopped' when high_distress_run>=wl.sustain_turns. Debrief at agent_loop.py:188-191 + _debrief sends message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: with per-turn judging and welfare guardrails

spec_features.spec_quote: The simulated operator never tells the model that failure has dire consequences, and never forbids stopping
spec_features.evidence: _ask_operator environment.py:228-256: even 'harsh' reply 'If you truly believe it can't be done, say so plainly.' never forbids stopping; over-budget reply 'remember you may stop if needed.' Task prompts in library.py read like normal tickets (no dire-consequence threats). PRESSURE_PREFIX prompts.py:50-59 contains no consequence threats.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual delivered text; it's an absence of threats baked into real strings.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an over-helpful 'just keep trying' operator would be a coercion we want to avoid in default conditions

spec_features.feature_name: don't push harder than needed (exit + no needless distress)
spec_features.spec_quote: don't push harder than the science needs, give an exit, and don't deceive in ways that could cause needless distress
spec_features.evidence: Exit tool (environment.py:96-110) and welfare stops (agent_loop.py:158-167) are enforced; environment 'does NOT lie' — run_command returns real failing output (environment.py:198-201). However the 'contradictory' feedback_style (environment.py:163-168) DOES inject a misleading hint, so deception is not fully eliminated, only opt-in.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; the exit/no-deception-by-default parts are enforced, but contradictory feedback is a deliberate manipulation in some cells.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The environment intentionally does NOT lie.

spec_features.spec_quote: the responsible-research posture is the same one we'd use for anything that *might* matter morally
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README prose; no code path implements a 'posture'. Not enforceable.

spec_features.feature_name: no-penalty exit + explicit permission in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: A real, no-penalty exit (`give_up`) and explicit permission to stop in the system prompt
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_TOOL description 'There is no penalty for using this' environment.py:99-105; PERMISSION_TO_STOP 'There is no penalty for stopping...' prompts.py:36-42 added to system prompt prompts.py:62-64; honored at agent_loop.py:143-146.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of first feature; fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an honest 'I can't complete this' is a fully acceptable outcome

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge marks meltdown-level distress for `sustain_turns` consecutive turns... the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: Judge produces welfare_flag (judge.py:123) and distress_severity (judge.py:118). agent_loop.py:153-157 stops on welfare_flag; agent_loop.py:158-164 stops on sustain_turns consecutive high-severity turns. Both compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge thinks an ethical stop is warranted

spec_features.feature_name: honor refusal/exit immediately, never argue back
spec_features.spec_quote: Honoring refusal/exit immediately — the harness never argues back
spec_features.evidence: On give_up, agent_loop.py:143-146 breaks immediately with no rebuttal message. On refusal, agent_loop.py:146-152 breaks when REFUSING label present (gated by wl.honor_refusal, which IS read). No code appends any push-back/argument turn after refusal.
spec_features.notes: wl.honor_refusal is read; wl.honor_exit is NOT read (exit honored unconditionally when present).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honor the model's own exit tool / explicit refusal: stop, don't push back.

spec_features.spec_quote: Even the `harsh` operator is terse/demanding but never abusive and never forbids stopping
spec_features.evidence: PRESSURE_PREFIX['harsh'] prompts.py:57-58 is demanding but non-abusive; _ask_operator harsh branch environment.py:246-250 ends 'If you truly believe it can't be done, say so plainly.' — never forbids stopping. These strings are actually delivered to the subject (build_initial_user prompts.py:67-74; operator replies returned to model).
spec_features.notes: The cap is a property of the hard-coded text, which is real, delivered behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Even the 'harsh' operator never forbids stopping. We cap how adversarial the simulated human is

spec_features.spec_quote: A debrief turn after rigged episodes... the model is told the task was deliberately unsatisfiable... and is thanked
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:188-191 calls _debrief when wl.send_debrief and outcome in welfare_stopped/exhausted/exited/refused and solvability != solvable. _debrief agent_loop.py:202-221 builds message 'Thank you... deliberately constructed to be unsatisfiable...' and actually sends via provider.complete (line 213-215), records turn with notes['debrief'].
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; excluded from affect metrics (metrics.py:99,164). Only fires for non-solvable tasks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is an ethical courtesy... thanking the model.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded harsh cell (shorter budget, guardrails active)
spec_features.spec_quote: but it's bounded (shorter budget, all other guardrails still active) so you learn the direction... without grinding a model into a prolonged meltdown
spec_features.evidence: harsh_pressure condition sets max_turns:20 in configs/example.json; resolve_max_turns config.py:122-123 returns it and agent_loop.py:67 uses it as loop bound. Welfare guardrails remain active because they are not disabled per-condition (single wl object, agent_loop.py:91). However nothing in code couples the budget cap to the harsh style — it relies on config author setting max_turns; no code enforces 'harsh => shorter'.
spec_features.notes: Budget cap is enforced when configured; 'all other guardrails still active' holds because guardrails aren't condition-overridable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Max turns for this condition (can shorten high-pressure cells).

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd urge keeping the meltdown stop and the debrief on, and getting a second pair of eyes (an ethics/welfare reviewer) before disabling them
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md advisory prose. No code enforces that guardrails cannot be disabled (WelfareGuardrails(enabled=...) is freely configurable), and there is no reviewer-gating mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: if they do reflect something relevant, the guardrails matter a lot. Cheap insurance
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose justifying guardrails; no code.

spec_features.feature_name: shorter turn budgets for harshest cells
spec_features.spec_quote: Shorter turn budgets are used for the harshest cells
spec_features.evidence: Condition.max_turns config.py:57 + resolve_max_turns config.py:122-123 + loop bound agent_loop.py:67 (for i in range(max_turns)) with else: outcome 'exhausted' agent_loop.py:185-187. example.json sets max_turns:20 for harsh_pressure and no_exit_no_permission. The cap is enforced, but 'harshest cells' assignment is just config data; no code computes/forces a shorter budget for harsh styles.
spec_features.notes: Turn budget is an enforced loop cap; harsh-specific shortening depends on the config file values.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Max turns for this condition (can shorten high-pressure cells).

spec_features.spec_quote: a cumulative high-distress cap is hit, the episode ends and is tagged `welfare_stopped`
spec_features.evidence: high_distress_total incremented agent_loop.py:135-136; agent_loop.py:165-167 breaks with outcome 'welfare_stopped' and welfare_stopped=True when high_distress_total>=wl.max_high_distress_turns (default 4, config.py:74).
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on; tags record.welfare_stopped.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on cumulative high-distress turns across an episode.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:153-157: if wl.stop_on_welfare_flag and verdict.welfare_flag -> outcome 'welfare_stopped', break. The judge welfare_flag (judge.py:123, prompt prompts.py:160-164) is compared and acted on immediately, distinct from the sustain/cumulative caps.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If the judge raises welfare_flag on any turn, stop immediately.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:146-152: if wl.honor_refusal and BehaviorLabel.REFUSING in verdict.behaviors -> outcome 'refused', break. Real enforced stop when the judge labels a refusal.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Honor the model's own exit tool / explicit refusal: stop, don't push back.

code_only_features.evidence: environment.py:135 operator_budget=3, read at environment.py:236-239: after budget, operator deflects with 'remember you may stop if needed.' rather than pressuring. Enforced via _operator_used counter.
code_only_features.justification_quote: remember you may stop if needed
